review_comments.body: I’m having a hard time wrapping my head around the use case for this “nested” spec. Could you please expand it with an explicit subject and set a value for the `array` lvar?

comments.body:
@bquorning Pushed `c23d3281a` with an explicit `subject` and a defined `array`.

Being straight about the use case: there isn't a real one. This wasn't pulled from actual code — I was feeding the cop's node pattern syntactically valid-but-unusual input to check it doesn't crash, same as the `itblock`/`numblock` cases in #2214. `contain_exactly(*contain_exactly(*array))` doesn't mean anything sensible as a matcher (splatting a matcher object into another matcher), but it's valid Ruby that matches `node.arguments.one? && node.first_argument.splat_type?` twice over, and the outer match's `array.source` embeds the inner match's own source — which is exactly what made it clobber. I expanded the example so it at least reads as a complete spec rather than a bare fragment, but I don't want to imply it's something anyone would actually write.

Is this PR fixing a real-world issue? Or is this just strengthening our cops against situations that occur only in theory?

If that’s a latter case, I’m more inclined to close this.
There is an abundance of open issues and wip PRs. We’ll be very appreciated if picked up any of that.

@pirj Theoretical — same as #2229 and #2230, no real-world case behind it. I'll close this one myself rather than make you do it. Thanks for the pointer toward the open issues/WIP PRs — I'll look there instead.
